accepted.expected_invariant: API health endpoint remains available or recovers within a short restart window without manual intervention.
accepted.hypothesis: Killing the api container will expose whether the healthcheck and restart policy are sufficient to maintain API availability during the restart window.
accepted.recovery_expectation: Docker restart policy should restart the container; healthcheck should pass after startup; cleanup is automatic.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify API health and mock workflow response. Inject: kill the api container. Observe: monitor health endpoint and workflow response during restart. Oracle: check that health returns to ready and workflow completes successfully after recovery.
accepted.weakness_surface: api service has a healthcheck and restart=always, but no replica redundancy; a single kill may cause a brief availability gap and potential request failures.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API and worker operations that rely on agent_backend remain functional or fail gracefully without cascading failures.
accepted.hypothesis: Killing the agent_backend container will expose whether the API and worker can tolerate the loss of the agent backend, given it has no healthcheck and depends on plugin_daemon and redis.
accepted.recovery_expectation: Restart policy should bring agent_backend back; dependent services should recover once it is available.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify mock workflow that uses agent_backend. Inject: kill agent_backend container. Observe: API responses and worker task execution. Oracle: check that requests either succeed after restart or return clear errors without system-wide failure.
accepted.weakness_surface: agent_backend has no healthcheck and restart=always; its absence may cause API requests that depend on it to fail or hang until restart completes.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API responses remain within acceptable latency and worker tasks are not dropped or delayed beyond a bounded threshold.
accepted.hypothesis: Introducing 500ms latency on the redis service will expose whether API, worker, and agent_backend timeouts are configured to handle slow cache/queue operations.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After removing the delay, latency should return to baseline and any queued tasks should process normally.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: measure API latency and workflow completion time. Inject: add 500ms latency to redis traffic. Observe: API response times and worker task completion. Oracle: check that API latency does not exceed a defined SLO and that tasks complete within a bounded time.
accepted.weakness_surface: redis is a critical dependency for api, agent_backend, worker, and worker_beat; added latency may cause request timeouts or queue processing delays.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API and worker database operations complete within a bounded time and do not cause cascading failures.
accepted.hypothesis: Adding 500ms latency to db_mysql will expose whether API and worker database timeouts are configured to handle slow queries or connection delays.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After removing the delay, database operations should return to normal latency and any pending work should complete.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify database-dependent workflow. Inject: add 500ms latency to db_mysql. Observe: API response times and worker task success. Oracle: check that requests either succeed within a defined timeout or fail gracefully without system-wide outage.
accepted.weakness_surface: db_mysql is a primary database for api, api_websocket, plugin_daemon, worker, and worker_beat; latency may cause connection pool exhaustion or request failures.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: Agent backend operations that use the proxy remain functional or fail with retryable errors, not permanent failures.
accepted.hypothesis: Introducing 50% packet loss on the agent_ssrf_proxy will expose whether the agent backend can tolerate unreliable outbound proxy connections.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After removing the loss, proxy traffic should return to normal and any retries should succeed.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify a workflow that uses the ssrf proxy. Inject: add 50% packet loss to agent_ssrf_proxy. Observe: success rate and error types of agent backend calls. Oracle: check that the system retries and eventually succeeds or returns clear errors without crashing.
accepted.weakness_surface: agent_ssrf_proxy has no healthcheck and restart=always; packet loss may cause intermittent failures in agent backend calls that rely on the proxy.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: Plugin-dependent operations remain available or fail gracefully without crashing the agent backend.
accepted.hypothesis: Introducing 50% packet loss on plugin_daemon will expose whether agent_backend and other dependents can handle unreliable plugin communication.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After removing the loss, plugin communication should return to normal and pending operations should complete.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: verify a plugin invocation workflow. Inject: add 50% packet loss to plugin_daemon. Observe: success rate and error handling. Oracle: check that failures are retried or reported cleanly, and no cascading failure occurs.
accepted.weakness_surface: plugin_daemon has no healthcheck and restart=always; packet loss may cause agent_backend to fail when invoking plugins.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: API health endpoint remains responsive and request latency stays within acceptable bounds under CPU stress.
accepted.hypothesis: Stressing the api container CPU to 80% will expose whether the service can maintain responsiveness under high load, given it has a healthcheck but no resource limits.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After stopping the stress, CPU usage should return to normal and latency should recover.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: measure API latency and health. Inject: stress api CPU to 80% for 30s. Observe: health endpoint and request latency. Oracle: check that health remains ready and latency does not exceed a defined threshold.
accepted.weakness_surface: api has no resource limits; CPU contention may cause healthcheck timeouts and degraded request handling.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response

accepted.expected_invariant: Worker tasks continue to be processed within a bounded delay and the worker remains healthy.
accepted.hypothesis: Stressing the worker container CPU to 80% will expose whether task processing can tolerate resource contention, given it has a healthcheck and restart=always.
accepted.recovery_expectation: After stopping the stress, task processing should return to normal speed and health should remain stable.
accepted.validation_plan: Baseline: submit a mock task and measure completion time. Inject: stress worker CPU to 80% for 30s. Observe: task completion time and worker health. Oracle: check that tasks complete within a defined timeout and worker health remains ready.
accepted.weakness_surface: worker has no resource limits; CPU stress may delay task processing and cause heartbeat or healthcheck failures.
accepted.workload_contract: API readiness plus mock workflow response
